newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: REAL AFRICA IN 450 MLN RAND RIGHTS ISSUES.
newsitem.headline: REAL AFRICA IN 450 MLN RAND RIGHTS ISSUES.

text.p: Real Africa Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that it planned a rights issue of new shares to raise 300 million rand.
In the same statement Real Africa Investments Ltd (Rail) said it planned a rights issue of new shares to raise 150 million rand.

"The purpose of the RAH rights offer is to raise capital in order to pay for acquisitions previously made, to fund increased shareholdings in existing underlying investments and to fund fututre investment opportunities," the firms said in a statement.
"The purpose of the RAI rights offer is to is to enable RAI to follow its rights in the RAH rights offer," it added.
Rail is a black empowerment investment vehicle.
The move is the latest in a flood of recent cash calls by some of South Africa's biggest firms hungry to tap investors for new funds.
Late in September three companies announced plans to raise cash on one day.
Drinks giant South African Breweries Ltd opened the show by saying it was considering an issue of up to 2.0 billion rand worth of new shares.

Just hours later, Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd (Amic) announced a rights issue to reap 1.2 billion rand and investment group NSA Investments Ltd said it wanted to net 280 million rand from the market.
